content:
lina: ACME tenant reporting sudden p95 jumps (200ms -> 1.8s) and intermittent 429s on their dedicated pool eu-west-1-ded-11 starting ~15:20 UTC. Customer says errors line up with their nightly batch run.

aj: On it. Can you paste pool id + tenant id? Any recent deploys?

lina: pool: pool-eu-ded-11 tenant: acme-fin-prod. Customer says no config changes. Sample API error lines:
```json
{ "ts": "2026-02-13T15:21:07Z", "code":429, "msg":"capacity exceeded", "model":"redwood/mosaic-8b" }
```
And a short tail from host metrics we got from the customer: 
```text
GPU0 MIG[0]: sm 98% memory 92% | GPU1 MIG[1]: sm 12% memory 18%
```

rahul: I pulled node metrics. One physical host has a tenant running large batched workloads on slice0 causing SM saturation + memory thrash. MIG slice0 is pegged; requests to slice0 are getting queued -> frontend returns 429s due to per-slice inflight caps.

rahul: Quick check commands to reproduce locally:
```
nvmldevicequery --gpu 0 --mig --stats
kubectl top pod -n dedicated-pool-eu --containers | grep acme
```

jo: FYI infra-autoscaler didn't trigger because eviction threshold was misread (we have a rounding bug; see PR #389). Autoscaler believes node has ~15% free vram but per-slice exhaustion still occurs. I'll patch a short-term rule: trigger spin-up when any slice >85% SM AND >80% mem.

sam: :eyes: we should offer immediate mitigation to customer (migrate acme to isolated node) and follow up with root cause + timeline. What's risk to other tenants during migration?

rahul: Migration low-risk if we move traffic to another physical with empty slices. Repro steps for eng-runtime to validate fix: run our loadgen with batched payloads to recreate SM saturation:
```
./sandbox/loadgen --model redwood/mosaic-8b --batch 32 --seq 512 --dur 60
```
That should cause 429s within ~20s on a crowded slice. Capture nvtop + perf counters.

aj: I pinged the customer with a migration window (start in 30m). They accepted. Taking ownership of migration + postmortem.

lina: :thumbsup: Action items:
- aj: run migration + monitor p95 and 429s
- rahul: run loadgen + collect nvtop/perf
- jo: hotfix autoscaler rule + create a follow-up ticket to revert after full fix
- sam: draft customer note
I'll move this thread to eng-oncall after migration.

infrabot: Scheduled migration job job-762 queued on infra-runner-3. Alerting set for p95 > 750ms or 5xx/429 rate > 0.5%.

aj: Migration started. Patching routes now... :rocket:

lina: Observed: p95 back to baseline after migration, 429s dropped to 0. Thanks team. Filing postmortem.
